decisions.reason: A reference class electrometer is a core, long-lived dosimetry instrument close to the established offer and featured as a flagship, so withdrawal within a year is very unlikely.
A CT image quality phantom extends the firm's imaging QA portfolio, was launched only recently, and has a dedicated page, so it fits the expansion into imaging QA.
Although the mammography phantom is farther from the core offer, it supports the flagship imaging QA line and phantoms are low-cost to keep, so an early withdrawal is unlikely.
The full field mammography phantom may overlap somewhat with Product D, which carries some consolidation risk, but it completes the mammography QA offering and was launched only in 2024.
The imaging QA instrument line is presented as a strategic flagship with several models, so the firm will keep investing in it rather than withdraw it.
